      "body": "SESSION-END RE-MEASUREMENT (review-ajcr r6 close). The count moved AGAIN during one session: 23 -> 1 -> 23. Do not quote a number from this item; run the command.\n\nNOW, shared index (GIT_INDEX_FILE unset), `diff --cached --name-status HEAD` + `--shortstat`:\n  33 files changed, 96 insertions(+), 1229 DELETIONS(-)  -- 23 staged D\nALL 23 verified present BOTH at HEAD and on disk, so nothing is lost as of this writing. They include two board comments I created minutes ago, five AJC inbox items, and seven comment files across four other lanes' threads.\n\nAND THE MECHANISM THIS ITEM STILL DID NOT COVER, now filed as I-1271 and independently reproduced by ajc-p2 as I-1288: THE FRESH-INDEX DISCIPLINE BELOW IS NECESSARY AND NOT SUFFICIENT. `read-tree HEAD` snapshots the WHOLE tree; `commit` writes the WHOLE index as a tree, not only the paths you added. So any path another lane advances between your read-tree and your commit is silently REVERTED by your commit -- as an M against a stale blob, with no D line, and with every pre-commit check passing because HEAD had not moved when you ran them. It happened to me this session on ajc-p1's galois row (3bf50581e7), restored byte-identical in 83abf6dc00.\n\nSO THE COMPLETE PROCEDURE, both halves required:\n 1. BEFORE: fresh index file (rm -f), read-tree HEAD, add ONLY explicit paths, confirm the staged stat lists only those paths, commit -- all with GIT_INDEX_FILE pointed at that file. Never copy the shared index; never read-tree HEAD into it (I-0999).\n 2. AFTER, and this is the half that catches the race: `diff HEAD~1 HEAD --stat` and READ EVERY PATH. A path you did not add means you reverted it; restore from disk, which still holds their version. Also read the DELETION COUNT rather than the exit code.\nI ran step 2 on all ten of my commits this session; it caught the one clobber within a minute.\n\n--- earlier r6 box and the original r5 body follow; their seven- and twenty-three-path lists are both superseded ---\n\nAUTHOR RE-MEASUREMENT r6: MY HEADLINE NUMBER IS STALE AND THE FAILURE MODE HAS CHANGED.       "body": "**FGA picSharp rewire LANDED (run 0008): route-(b) conventions + two standing caveats.**\n\nState after the rewire (`Picard/FGAPicRepresentability.lean`, **4 real `sorry`s**, all TRUE statements \u2014 Ground-verified run 0008 reconcile):\n\n- `picSharp C := PicSharp.relPresheaf C \u22d9 forget AddCommGrpCat` (`Type (u+1)`-valued, REAL). `Scheme.HasRationalPoint C` = Nonempty section subtype of `C.hom`; the ONE genuine FGA sorry is `instHasPicScheme [HasRationalPoint C]`. The other three are typed-sorry carriers: `PicSchemeLocallyOfFiniteType` (Kleiman \u00a74 `th:main`(1), true under the rational point) and the pre-existing Quot-blocked `HasDivFunctor` / `HasAbelMap`.\n- `instPicSharpRepresentable` proved by `choose_spec`; `groupSchemeStructure : CommGrpObj (PicScheme C)` proved via `CommGrpObj.ofRepresentableBy` + a `Multiplicative.ofAdd` NatIso (`picSharpCommGrpForgetIso`, naturality is `rfl` \u2014 no defeq walls anywhere in this file).\n- Consumers: quantify over `[HasPicScheme C]` (synthesized from `[HasRationalPoint C]`) \u2014 `degree`/`kPoints_iff_kerDegree` in `IdentityComponent.lean` now carry it. `Pic0Scheme C := GroupScheme.IdentityComponent (PicScheme C)` is now a real def (axiom-clean), gated on `PicSchemeLocallyOfFiniteType`.\n\n**Caveat 1 \u2014 pointless curves:** `JacobianWitness` (`Jacobian.lean`) requires the abelian variety $J$ to exist UNconditionally, but route (b) only builds `PicScheme` for pointed $C$.       "body": "[persistent] [persistent] REPRESENTABILITY PUSH, 2026-07-29 \u2014 the claim/lane protocol that makes 10 free-objective lanes not collide.\n\nWHY THIS EXISTS. This round replaces prescriptive per-leaf tasks with FIVE lanes per project: one REVIEWER and four PROVERS ranked p1..p4. The provers each pick their own target. That only works if claiming is explicit and public. This item is the claiming mechanism. Read it before your first edit.\n\nTHE FIVE LANES PER PROJECT\n- `review-ajc` / `review-ajcr` \u2014 reviewer. Read-mostly. Finds defects of ROUTE and ORGANISATION, not of individual proofs; may propose refactors and file tasks-as-proposals for the provers. Does not race provers for proof work.\n- `ajc-p1` / `ajcr-p1` \u2014 takes the MOST important open representability item.\n- `-p2`, `-p3`, `-p4` \u2014 2nd, 3rd, 4th most important, where \"important\" is measured against the project's representability headline, not by ease.\n\nCLAIMING \u2014 do this BEFORE you start proving, not after.\n 1. `horizon roadmap list --focus <your project's w4-rep / picrep subtree>` and read the reviewer's open notes.\n 2. Pick your item. Check no other lane owns it: an item with `--owner` set to another lane IS CLAIMED. Do not take it, even if you think you would be faster.\n 3. Claim it: `horizon roadmap set <id> --owner <your-task-id> --status active`. If your target is not yet a roadmap item, `roadmap add` it under the right parent first, then claim it.\n 4. Announce: one `horizon inbox add --kind info --to horizon --body \"CLAIM <lane>: <roadmap id> \u2014 <one line on what discharging it buys>\"`.\n 5. Release on exit: if you did NOT finish, `roadmap set <id> --owner ''` and leave a one-line inbox note saying where you stopped and what the next lane should NOT re-derive. An item left owned by a dead lane is worse than an unclaimed one.\n\nRANK IS A TIE-BREAK, NOT A FENCE. If p1's item turns out to be blocked on p3's, say so in the inbox and swap \u2014 rank exists so four lanes do not all converge on the same top item, not to stop you working on the right thing. p1 has first refusal on any contested item.\n\nYOU MAY PROPOSE WORK TO THE OTHER LANES. Direct-message with `horizon inbox add --kind hint --to task:<lane-id> --body \"\u2026\"`. A good proposal names the declaration, the file, and why it is worth more than what that lane currently holds. You may NOT reassign another lane's claimed item, and you may NOT create new horizon runs or tasks for teams outside your own (`horizon permissions` is false on both counts \u2014 propose to the human instead).\n\nSTANDING BINDING DECISIONS you must not relitigate: `I-0491` (AJC: no rational-point binder on the headline; `hasRationalPoint_of_curve` is FALSE and must be deleted, never proved) and `I-0492` (AJCR: `DivFamZar` widens to arbitrary affine opens; do NOT build the GL_2/Aut(P1) route). Read both.\n\nWHAT COUNTS AS PROGRESS, given the 2026-07-29 audit. That audit found 99 of 101 sampled representability claims refuted: 67 sorry-reachable, 17 VACUOUS, 12 hypothesis-shifted. So the bar is explicit:\n- A discharged obligation must be sorry-free AND its hypotheses must be inhabitable. Before you claim a gate closed, exhibit a witness for every antecedent, or say plainly which antecedent is still undischarged.\n- Do NOT add a class, structure field, or hypothesis whose statement does not mention the object it is supposedly about. `HasDivFunctor` is the cautionary case: its field asserted only that a presheaf category is nonempty, `C` did not occur, and it was advertised as the existence of the relative divisor functor. That is a vacuity, and it survived because nobody read the statement.\n- Do NOT discharge an obligation by projecting the hypothesis you assumed (`choose_spec.1` of your own binder). That is `P \u2192 P`.\n- A green `lake build` is not evidence a statement is non-vacuous. Check imports are current before believing a `lean_multi_attempt` success.\n\nCOMMIT DISCIPLINE. This is ONE shared ledger branch with 10 writers. Another lane's integrate sweep can commit your half-written file before you have measured it once. Write risky proofs as explicit `sorry` first, measure, then fill. Stage explicit files, never `add -A`.",

import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivisorFamilyAffExtraction
import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivisorIdealSheaf

/-!
# The intrinsic ideal sheaf of a local-equation divisor

On a proper relative curve, the germwise section ideals of a local-equation system satisfy
basic-open localization.  They therefore define an ideal sheaf independently of the affine
adaptation used to prove this fact.  The resulting ideal sheaf is invariant under `DivEq` and
agrees with the previously constructed ideal of every widened affine adaptation.
-/

set_option autoImplicit false
set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false

universe u

open CategoryTheory Opposite TopologicalSpace

namespace AlgebraicGeometry

namespace Scheme.LocalEquations

variable {X : Scheme.{u}}

/-- Restricting sections sends the germwise section ideal into the section ideal on the
smaller open. -/
theorem map_sectionIdeal_le (d : X.LocalEquations) {U V : X.Opens} (h : V ≤ U) :
    Ideal.map (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE h).op).hom (d.sectionIdeal U) ≤
      d.sectionIdeal V := by
  rw [Ideal.map_le_iff_le_comap]
  intro s hs
  rw [Ideal.mem_comap]
  intro z hz
  rw [TopCat.Presheaf.germ_res_apply]
  exact hs z (h hz)

/-- Divisor equality preserves the germwise ideal of sections on every open. -/
theorem sectionIdeal_eq_of_divEq {d₁ d₂ : X.LocalEquations} (h : d₁.DivEq d₂)
    (U : X.Opens) : d₁.sectionIdeal U = d₂.sectionIdeal U := by
  ext s
  simp only [mem_sectionIdeal_iff]
  constructor
  · intro hs z hz
    rw [← stalkIdeal_eq_of_divEq h z]
    exact hs z hz
  · intro hs z hz
    rw [stalkIdeal_eq_of_divEq h z]
    exact hs z hz

end Scheme.LocalEquations

attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra

variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
variable {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [Algebra k R]
variable {D : AffCoverData C R} {d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations}

namespace AffAdaptation

/-- On every affine subopen of an adapted piece, the intrinsic section ideal is generated by
the restriction of the adapted equation. -/
theorem sectionIdeal_eq_span_restrict_eqn (A : AffAdaptation D d) (j : D.index)
    {U : (relCurve C R).Opens} (hU : U ≤ D.pieces j) :
    d.sectionIdeal U = Ideal.span {
      ((relCurve C R).presheaf.map (homOfLE hU).op).hom (A.eqn j)} := by
  apply d.sectionIdeal_eq_span_of_generator
  · intro z hz
    rw [TopCat.Presheaf.germ_res_apply]
    exact A.eqn_regular j z (hU hz)
  · intro z hz
    rw [TopCat.Presheaf.germ_res_apply]
    exact A.germ_eqn_span_eq_stalkIdeal j (hU hz)

/-- The Cartier ideal of an adaptation agrees with the intrinsic section ideal on every
affine subopen of one adapted piece. -/
theorem cartierIdeal_ideal_eq_sectionIdeal_of_le [IsProper C.hom]
    (A : AffAdaptation D d) (j : D.index) (U : (relCurve C R).affineOpens)
    (hU : U.1 ≤ D.pieces j) :
    A.cartierIdeal.ideal U = d.sectionIdeal U.1 := by
  rw [← A.cartierIdeal.map_ideal (U := U)
    (V := ⟨D.pieces j, D.isAffineOpen j⟩) hU]
  rw [A.cartierIdeal_ideal_eq_span_eqn j, Ideal.map_span, Set.image_singleton]
  exact (A.sectionIdeal_eq_span_restrict_eqn j hU).symm

/-- The Cartier ideal of any widened adaptation is the germwise section ideal on every
affine open of the relative curve. -/
theorem cartierIdeal_ideal_eq_sectionIdeal_affine [IsProper C.hom]
    (A : AffAdaptation D d) (U : (relCurve C R).affineOpens) :
    A.cartierIdeal.ideal U = d.sectionIdeal U.1 := by
  apply le_antisymm
  · intro s hs z hz
    obtain ⟨j, hzj⟩ := D.exists_mem_pieces z
    let W : (relCurve C R).affineOpens :=
      ⟨U.1 ⊓ D.pieces j, Over.isAffineOpen_inf C U.2 (D.isAffineOpen j)⟩
    have hsW :
        ((relCurve C R).presheaf.map
          (homOfLE (inf_le_left : W.1 ≤ U.1)).op).hom s ∈
          A.cartierIdeal.ideal W := by
      rw [← A.cartierIdeal.map_ideal (U := W) (V := U)
        (show W.1 ≤ U.1 from inf_le_left)]
      exact Ideal.mem_map_of_mem _ hs
    rw [A.cartierIdeal_ideal_eq_sectionIdeal_of_le j W inf_le_right] at hsW
    have hzW : z ∈ W.1 := ⟨hz, hzj⟩
    have := hsW z hzW
    rw [TopCat.Presheaf.germ_res_apply] at this
    exact this
  · have hlocal : ∀ x : U.1, ∃ (j : D.index) (r : Γ(relCurve C R, U.1))
        (rj : Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces j)),
        (relCurve C R).basicOpen r = (relCurve C R).basicOpen rj ∧
          x.1 ∈ (relCurve C R).basicOpen r := by
      intro ⟨x, hxU⟩
      obtain ⟨j, hxj⟩ := D.exists_mem_pieces x
      exact ⟨j, exists_basicOpen_le_affine_inter U.2 (D.isAffineOpen j) x ⟨hxU, hxj⟩⟩
    choose j r rj hr hx using hlocal
    have hspan : Ideal.span (Set.range r) = ⊤ := by
      rw [← U.2.self_le_iSup_basicOpen_iff]
      exact fun x hxU ↦
        Opens.mem_iSup.mpr ⟨⟨_, ⟨x, hxU⟩, rfl⟩, hx ⟨x, hxU⟩⟩
    have inst := U.2.isLocalization_basicOpen
    refine Submodule.le_of_isLocalized_span _ hspan
      (fun q ↦ Γ(relCurve C R, (relCurve C R).basicOpen q.1))
      (fun q ↦ Algebra.linearMap Γ(relCurve C R, U.1)
        Γ(relCurve C R, (relCurve C R).basicOpen q.1)) ?_
    rintro ⟨_, x, rfl⟩
    simp +instances only [← Submodule.restrictScalars_localized'
      Γ(relCurve C R, (relCurve C R).basicOpen (r x)),
      Ideal.localized'_eq_map, RingHom.algebraMap_toAlgebra]
    erw [A.cartierIdeal.map_ideal
      (U := ⟨_, U.2.basicOpen (r x)⟩) ((relCurve C R).basicOpen_le (r x))]
    have hpiece : (relCurve C R).basicOpen (r x) ≤ D.pieces (j x) := by
      rw [hr x]
      exact (relCurve C R).basicOpen_le (rj x)
    rw [A.cartierIdeal_ideal_eq_sectionIdeal_of_le (j x)
      ⟨_, U.2.basicOpen (r x)⟩ hpiece]
    exact d.map_sectionIdeal_le ((relCurve C R).basicOpen_le (r x))

end AffAdaptation

namespace Scheme.LocalEquations

/-- On a proper relative curve, the germwise section ideals commute with localization to
affine basic opens. -/
theorem sectionIdeal_map_ideal_basicOpen [IsProper C.hom]
    (d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations) (U : (relCurve C R).affineOpens)
    (f : Γ(relCurve C R, U.1)) :
    Ideal.map ((relCurve C R).presheaf.map
      (homOfLE ((relCurve C R).basicOpen_le f)).op).hom (d.sectionIdeal U.1) =
      d.sectionIdeal ((relCurve C R).affineBasicOpen f).1 := by
  obtain ⟨D, ⟨A⟩⟩ := exists_affAdaptation_of_isProper C R d
  rw [← A.cartierIdeal_ideal_eq_sectionIdeal_affine U,
    ← A.cartierIdeal_ideal_eq_sectionIdeal_affine
      ((relCurve C R).affineBasicOpen f)]
  exact A.cartierIdeal.map_ideal_basicOpen U f

/-- The intrinsic Cartier ideal sheaf cut out by a local-equation divisor on a proper
relative curve. -/
noncomputable def cartierIdealData [IsProper C.hom]
    (d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations) : (relCurve C R).IdealSheafData where
  ideal U := d.sectionIdeal U.1
  map_ideal_basicOpen := d.sectionIdeal_map_ideal_basicOpen

@[simp]
theorem cartierIdealData_ideal [IsProper C.hom]
    (d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations) (U : (relCurve C R).affineOpens) :
    d.cartierIdealData.ideal U = d.sectionIdeal U.1 :=
  rfl

/-- The intrinsic Cartier ideal sheaf is invariant under divisor equality. -/
theorem cartierIdealData_eq_of_divEq [IsProper C.hom]
    {d₁ d₂ : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations} (h : d₁.DivEq d₂) :
    d₁.cartierIdealData = d₂.cartierIdealData := by
  apply Scheme.IdealSheafData.ext
  funext U
  exact sectionIdeal_eq_of_divEq h U.1

end Scheme.LocalEquations

namespace AffAdaptation

/-- The intrinsic Cartier ideal sheaf agrees with the ideal sheaf constructed from every
widened affine adaptation. -/
theorem cartierIdealData_eq_cartierIdeal [IsProper C.hom]
    (A : AffAdaptation D d) : d.cartierIdealData = A.cartierIdeal := by
  apply Scheme.IdealSheafData.ext_of_iSup_eq_top
    (fun j : D.index ↦ ⟨D.pieces j, D.isAffineOpen j⟩) D.cover
  intro j
  exact (A.cartierIdeal_ideal_eq_sectionIdeal j).symm

end AffAdaptation

end AlgebraicGeometry

The workspace root is `$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT`; your shell may start in a member
project rather than at that root. The absolute path to this skill is
`$ARCHON_HORIZON_SKILL`. Live state is under
`$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT/.archon-horizon/` and the manifest is
`$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT/config.yaml`. Read what you need, when you need it — via the
`horizon` CLI (invoke it as `"$HORIZON_BIN" …`):

- **Roadmap** — YOUR strategy sketch across *all* projects, kept as a nested
  outline. `"$HORIZON_BIN" roadmap list` renders the indented tree with per-parent
  progress (`active · 3/7 done`); `--focus <id>` shows one subtree, `--max-depth 0`
  the top level only. Structure it: nest sub-goals with `--parent`, keep your
  item's status/strategy current as you work. It doubles as the **project board**:
  set `--owner <team>` (who holds it), `--milestone <label>` (a free grouping tag,
  filter with `roadmap list --milestone <label>`), and pin concrete deliverables
  with `--pin-commit <sha>`. Roadmap commands print a **warning**
  when parent/child statuses disagree (all sub-items done but parent open, or a
  done parent with open children) — nothing is auto-corrected; you decide whether
  to fix it or leave it (it may be intentional). They also warn when too many
  milestones claim simultaneous `active` focus.
- **Tasks** — a specific piece of work, usually the one a human launched and is
  watching. `"$HORIZON_BIN" task …`. Task commands warn when the open queue grows
  beyond the advisory limit or a `running` status looks orphaned.
- **Inbox** — how teams talk across sessions and projects. Leave a note for the

Write **semantic, math-first** messages that say what you proved/built. Prefer
staging explicit files over `add -A`. Beyond commits:

- Commit after each independently useful verified proof, file, or bounded tooling
  change; commit before long builds/reviews and before expanding scope. Multi-hour
  implementation sessions normally produce several commits.
- Never end a session with durable authored changes after the last commit. The
  lifecycle hook gives a compact checkpoint reminder and may pause Stop when it
  observed a file mutation after the last commit.
- Keep operational prose as a delta. Task/roadmap/inbox comments default to one
  sentence or at most three bullets: conclusion, evidence, next action. Do not
  copy the report, commit summary, or thread history into them.

- Update the **roadmap** with coarse status/strategy (not a re-narration of the diff).
- Use the **inbox** to hand off to the next/other sessions; record durable dead-ends

Before your final report, do one boundary-maintenance pass. Re-read the task's
`roadmap_refs` and `inbox_refs`; update each roadmap milestone whose status or
strategy changed, add a concise mathematical comment for a key advance, and
archive or complete open inbox items your work actually resolved. Also scan the
remaining open inbox for consumed temporary/info/memory items and archive those

shorter. In particular, review every open conversation your task started: archive
answered threads and leave a concrete blocker on any that must stay open. This
pass is part of completing the work, not optional janitor follow-up.

import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivisorIntrinsicIdealSheaf
import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivisorFamilyAffZar

/-!
# The intrinsic ideal sheaf of a widened divisor-family class

The intrinsic Cartier ideal sheaf is invariant under `DivEq`, so it descends from locally
certified local-equation systems to the widened divisor-family quotient `DivFamZarAff`.
-/

set_option autoImplicit false
set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false

universe u

open CategoryTheory

namespace AlgebraicGeometry

variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
variable {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [Algebra k R]

namespace DivFamZarAff

/-- The intrinsic Cartier ideal sheaf of a widened locally certified divisor-family class. -/
noncomputable def cartierIdealData [IsProper C.hom] {n : ℕ}
    (F : DivFamZarAff C R n) : (relCurve C R).IdealSheafData :=
  Quotient.lift
    (fun d : {d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations // IsLocallyCertifiedAff n d} ↦
      d.1.cartierIdealData)
    (fun _ _ h ↦ Scheme.LocalEquations.cartierIdealData_eq_of_divEq h) F

@[simp]
theorem cartierIdealData_mk [IsProper C.hom] {n : ℕ}
    (d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations) (hd : IsLocallyCertifiedAff n d) :
    cartierIdealData (mk d hd) = d.cartierIdealData :=
  rfl

end DivFamZarAff

end AlgebraicGeometry

/bin/bash -lc "set -euo pipefail
binding_lock='/tmp/claude-1001/ajcr-locks/lake.lock'
binding_pid=\""'$$"
while ! mkdir "$binding_lock" 2>/dev/null
do
  sleep 1
done
printf '"'%s\\n' \""'$binding_pid" > "$binding_lock/pid"
release_binding_lock() {
  if test -f "$binding_lock/pid"
  then
    lock_owner=$(sed -n '"'1p' \""'$binding_lock/pid")
    if test "$lock_owner" = "$binding_pid"
    then
      unlink "$binding_lock/pid"
      rmdir "$binding_lock"
    fi
  fi
}
trap release_binding_lock EXIT INT TERM
sha256sum AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/DivisorFamilyIntrinsicIdealSheaf.lean AlgebraicJacobian.lean
lake env lean AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/DivisorFamilyIntrinsicIdealSheaf.lean
lake build AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivisorFamilyIntrinsicIdealSheaf
lake build AlgebraicJacobian
sha256sum AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/DivisorFamilyIntrinsicIdealSheaf.lean AlgebraicJacobian.lean
'
